title: Generator torsor and tautological ample module of a principal log ideal
statement:
Let $p:(X,M,\alpha)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a fine log scheme over the spectrum of a commutative ring $A$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]. Let $\mathcal J\subset M$ be a locally principal log ideal generated by a finite nonempty family of global sections $(h_e)_{e\in E}$. Assume that the locus $V_e$ where $h_e$ generates $\mathcal J$ on geometric stalks is a Zariski open affine subscheme of $X$, and that these loci cover $X$. Its sheaf of generators is a torsor under $M^\times=\mathcal O_X^\times$: the action is addition of a unit and between two generators there is a unique such unit. There is a canonically associated invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with frame $v_e$ on $V_e$ and transition
$$v_f=\alpha(h_f-h_e)v_e\quad\text{on }V_e\cap V_f.$$
For every $h\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal J)$ there is a global section $s_h$ of $L$ with formula $s_h=\alpha(h-h_e)v_e$ on $V_e$. Its nonvanishing locus is exactly the locus where $h$ generates $\mathcal J$; in particular $X_{s_{h_e}}=V_e$. The module $L$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] and is relatively ample over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, meaning that its restriction over every affine open of the base is ample. Under every affine base change $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the corresponding pulled-back line bundle and sections have the same generator-locus description and are ample. Log isomorphisms identifying the locally principal ideals identify their generator torsors, line bundles and sections canonically, independently of the chosen finite generating families; these identifications respect identities, composition and further base change.

proof.text: Fine charts give cancellation in the geometric stalks of $M$. Here is the elementary check, also useful after base change. In a chart $P\to B$, put $F=\beta^{-1}(B^\times)$. Localize $P$ by $F$, obtaining $R=P+(-F)\subset P^{\rm gp}$, and put $H=F^{\rm gp}\subset R^\times$. The chart pushout is $(R\oplus B^\times)/H$, where $t\in H$ identifies $(r+t,u)$ with $(r,\beta(t)u)$. Since $H$ is a group of units, equality in this quotient is exactly equality after one such translation. If two pairs become equal after addition of a common pair, cancel its $R$-component in $P^{\rm gp}$ and its unit component in $B^\times$; they were already equal. Thus this pushout is integral. The chart-stalk formula in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and the integral charts in [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum] prove the assertion, without saturation or Noetherian hypotheses.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, printed pp.107--108; agent expansion of principal-ideal cancellation and strict descent

proof.text: If $a,b$ generate the same principal ideal in an integral monoid, write $b=a+c$ and $a=b+d$. Cancellation gives $c+d=0$, so $c$ is a unit, and cancellation also makes $c$ unique. Conversely a unit translate is again a generator. Apply this at every geometric stalk. On $V_e$, every section $h$ of $\mathcal J$ has a unique difference $m_{h,e}$ with $h=h_e+m_{h,e}$: membership in the generated ideal gives these differences etale locally, and uniqueness glues them in the monoid sheaf. The generators form the subsheaf $T\subset\mathcal J$ of sections generating on all geometric stalks. The map $\mathcal O_X^\times\to T|_{V_e}$, $u\mapsto h_e+u$, is a sheaf isomorphism by the log unit axiom and the preceding calculation. It identifies addition of units with translation, proving the torsor assertion of [def-sc-gm-torsor], on both the etale site and its Zariski restriction.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, printed pp.107--108; agent expansion of principal-ideal cancellation and strict descent

proof.text: On $V_e\cap V_f$, put $u_{ef}=h_f-h_e$ and $g_{ef}=\alpha(u_{ef})\in\mathcal O_X^\times$. Uniqueness of differences gives $u_{ee}=0$, $u_{fe}=-u_{ef}$ and $u_{eg}=u_{ef}+u_{fg}$. Hence $g_{ee}=1$, $g_{fe}=g_{ef}^{-1}$ and $g_{eg}=g_{ef}g_{fg}$. Apply [lem-sc-glue-component-transition-cocycle] to the trivial rank-one modules on the Zariski cover $(V_e)$. Use the inverse scalar $g_{ef}^{-1}$ for the coordinate map from chart $e$ to chart $f$; equivalently its frames satisfy $v_f=g_{ef}v_e$. The result is an invertible module $L$, unique with these framed identifications.

source.place: Tag 00AM, lemma-glue-sheaves-structures; scalar cocycle specialization as in the cited node

proof.text: For $h\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal J)$ set $a_{h,e}=\alpha(m_{h,e})$. On an overlap, $m_{h,e}=m_{h,f}+u_{ef}$, so $a_{h,e}=a_{h,f}g_{ef}$. Consequently $a_{h,f}v_f=a_{h,e}v_e$. The sheaf axiom glues these sections uniquely to $s_h\in\Gamma(X,L)$, with precisely the required formula. In the frame $v_e$, the section is nonzero in the residue fibre at $x$ exactly when $a_{h,e}$ is a unit in the local ring. The log unit axiom identifies this with $m_{h,e}$ being a unit in the geometric log stalk; by Step 2 this is equivalent to $h$ generating the ideal there. Unit membership can be tested in the etale local rings, so this is the same nonvanishing locus as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. In particular $X_{s_{h_e}}=V_e$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, printed pp.107--108; agent expansion of principal-ideal cancellation and strict descent

proof.text: Every $V_e$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Given any open covering of $X$, choose a finite subcover of each $V_e$ and take their union; finiteness of $E$ makes this a finite subcover of $X$. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact. For each $x$ choose $e$ with $x\in V_e=X_{s_{h_e}}$. These are affine nonvanishing loci of sections of $L$ itself (power $n=1$). The two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] now prove absolute ampleness directly; no criterion requiring properness or a field is used.

The morphism $p$ is quasi-compact. Indeed, for any affine open $W\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$, each $V_e\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], so its inverse image of $W$ is affine and hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The finitely many inverse images cover $p^{-1}(W)$, and the finite-subcover argument of Step 5 applies. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] to $p$, $L$, and the one-member affine covering $\{\operatorname{Spec}A\}$. Its hypotheses are the quasi-compactness just proved and Step 5's ampleness. Its conclusion is ampleness over every affine open of the base, as required.

Let $q:X'=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], $L'=q^*L$ is invertible with pulled-back frames $v'_e$ and sections $s'_h=q^*s_h$; their formulas are obtained by applying $q^\sharp$ to $g_{ef}$ and $a_{h,e}$. Clause (3) of that node gives $(s'_h)(x')=s_h(q(x'))\otimes1$ in the extended residue field. A scalar in a field remains nonzero under a field extension, so $X'_{s'_h}=q^{-1}(X_{s_h})$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change] to Step 6. It gives relative ampleness of $L'$; taking the whole affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ gives absolute ampleness as well.

For the generator interpretation in Step 7 use the strict pulled-back log structure (the log structure associated to the inverse-image prelog structure). At a geometric $x'$ over $x$, take a fine chart $P$ near $x$ and its pulled-back chart in $\mathcal O_{X',\bar x'}$. Its stalk is the same unit pushout of Step 1, now with this new local ring. It is integral by the explicit cancellation there. On $q^{-1}(V_e)$ the image $h'_e$ still generates the image ideal, since every original ideal element is locally $h_e+m$. For each original global $h$, the difference from $h'_e$ is the image of $m_{h,e}$, and its structural scalar is $q^\sharp(a_{h,e})$. By the log unit axiom this difference is a unit exactly where this scalar is a unit; by Step 2 this is precisely the locus where $h'$ generates the pulled-back ideal. Thus the frames and sections of Step 7 have the claimed generator-locus meaning. In particular the distinguished loci are $q^{-1}(V_e)$. This argument also explains the phrase corresponding pulled-back line bundle: its transition functions are those of the pulled-back ideal, not a newly chosen polarization.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, printed pp.107--108; agent expansion of principal-ideal cancellation and strict descent

proof.text: To compare a second generating cover $(W_i,k_i)$ with $(V_e,h_e)$, on $V_e\cap W_i$ write $k_i=h_e+t_{ei}$, where Step 2 makes $t_{ei}$ a unique unit. Map its frame $w_i$ to $\alpha(t_{ei})v_e$. If $k_j=k_i+t_{ij}$ and $h_f=h_e+u_{ef}$, cancellation gives $t_{ej}=t_{ei}+t_{ij}$ and $t_{ei}=u_{ef}+t_{fi}$. These identities show that the local linear maps agree in both indices. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] glues them uniquely; the maps with reciprocal scalars glue to the inverse. For every $h$, the equality $h-h_e=(h-k_i)+t_{ei}$ shows that this isomorphism preserves $s_h$. For a log isomorphism $(f,\phi):(X,M)\to(Y,N)$, $\phi:f^{-1}N\simeq M$, with $\phi(f^{-1}\mathcal K)=\mathcal J$ and a generating family $(W_i,k_i)$ of $\mathcal K$: since $\phi$ is a stalkwise monoid isomorphism, $(f^{-1}W_i,\phi(k_i))$ generates $\mathcal J$ with the same loci, and $a\mapsto\phi(a)$ is the torsor map. As $\phi$ commutes with the structure maps, $f^\sharp\alpha_N(k_j-k_i)=\alpha_M(\phi(k_j)-\phi(k_i))$, so $f^*L_{\mathcal K}$ with frames $f^*w_i$ has the transitions of the transported family and $f^*s_k=s_{\phi(k)}$; uniqueness in Step 3 identifies it with that family's module, and the comparison above finishes. Identity comparisons have scalar $1$; composition multiplies the scalars because differences add. Applying $q^\sharp$ preserves these equalities, and the composition isomorphism for module pullback in [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies successive pulled-back frames. Uniqueness in the same gluing clause therefore proves the identity, composition and further-base-change compatibilities, independently of the generating families. Lean implementation (C3, 2026-10-26): the identity and composition clauses are now proved without an additional existence lemma. Transpose both comparison maps under the section-normalized tensor-pullback adjunction. To compare the transposes, choose a generator open around each point from hcover; every section on a smaller open is a scalar multiple of the restricted frame by LogIdealPolarization.frame. Naturality and linearity reduce equality to the values of those frames, and sheaf separation on intersections with the generator cover gives global equality. For identity, the relative test map is the identity and the left-adjoint-uniqueness unit equation identifies the normalized comparison. For composition, eliminate the equality of underlying base maps, use the CompEq equation on the three restricted-open test objects, the left-adjoint-uniqueness unit equation for tensorPullbackSectionComp, and naturality of the adjunction unit. Respects for the two factors then gives Respects for the composite on each frame. The torsor transport and strict-comparison existence portions of this step, and steps 1--8, remain the proof plan for the three untouched holes.

e : P.line ≅ Q.line, ∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : {s : logOpenSections M U // s ∈ J (Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι)}), e.hom.app U (P.value U s) = Q.value U s) ∧ (∀ (A' : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : Spec A' ⟶ Spec A), ∃ (N : EtaleLogStructure (pullback p g)) (q : EtaleLogMap N M), q.base = pullback.fst p g ∧ q.IsStrict ∧ N.IsFine ∧ N.IsInvertibleIdeal (q.pullbackIdeal J) ∧ (∃ hi : ((tensorPullback q.base).obj P.line).IsInvertible, @IsAmple (pullback p g) ((tensorPullback q.base).obj P.line) hi) ∧ (∀ s : {s : logOpenSections M ⊤ // s ∈ J (Scheme.Etale.mk (⊤ : X.Opens).ι)}, logIdealGeneratorLocus N (q.pullbackIdeal J) (logIdealPullSection q ⊤ s.val) = q.base ⁻¹' logIdealGeneratorLocus M J s.val) ∧ ∃ Q : LogIdealPolarization N (q.pullbackIdeal J), IsAmple (pullback p g) Q.line ∧ Q.RelativelyAmple (pullback.snd p g) ∧ (∀ s : {s : logOpenSections M ⊤ // s ∈ J (Scheme.Etale.mk (⊤ : X.Opens).ι)}, nonvanishingLocus ((tensorPullback q.base).obj P.line) (tensorPullbackSection q.base P.line ⊤ (P.value ⊤ s)) = q.base ⁻¹' logIdealGeneratorLocus M J s.val) ∧ ∃! e : (tensorPullback q.base).obj P.line ≅ Q.line, P.Respects Q q e)
